strengths: The combination of class-wise feature prototypes and class-specific BatchNorm matching provides a practical extension of SRe²L that avoids differentiating through student training and operates at ImageNet-1K scale.

Table I demonstrates meaningful improvements over the strengthened SRe²L baseline. ImageNet-1K accuracy increases from 54.4% to 57.6% at 50 images per class and from 58.3% to 60.7% at 100 images per class. Improvements also occur on ImageNette and Tiny ImageNet.

The authors transparently report a substantially improved reproduction of SRe²L and disclose the relevant hyperparameter changes. This strengthens the principal comparison. The dependence on SRe²L, DeepInversion, existing barycenter algorithms, and POT is acknowledged.

The experiments include multiple condensation budgets, component ablations, regularization sensitivity, and architecture transfer. Transfer within the ResNet family is encouraging: ImageNet-1K synthetic data achieve 62.2% with ResNet-101 at 50 images per class.
weaknesses: The central Wasserstein contribution is insufficiently distinguished from feature clustering. Equation 4 approximates one empirical distribution with a limited number of atoms. With squared Euclidean transport cost and freely optimized atom weights, its unregularized form reduces to the k-means/vector-quantization objective. A matched k-means prototype baseline is therefore essential to establish the added value of the proposed machinery. The claimed superiority over MMD also lacks a comparison holding the feature extractor and regularization fixed.

The ablations attribute much of the improvement to class-specific BatchNorm rather than the headline Wasserstein component. In Table III, keeping cross-entropy and class-specific BatchNorm fixed, adding the barycenter loss changes accuracy by −0.1, +0.8, and +0.5 percentage points on ImageNette, Tiny ImageNet, and ImageNet-1K, respectively. These are modest effects, and corresponding ablations at 50 and 100 images per class are missing.

The connection between the optimized distribution and the delivered dataset is incomplete. Equation 3 and the appendix optimize nonuniform atom weights, but these weights disappear from Equation 5, Algorithm 1's output, and the downstream training description. Representing every support point once generally does not preserve the optimized weighted distribution. The paper should explain how these weights affect sampling or training, or explicitly impose uniform weights.

Important details of the central solver remain unspecified. The main text states that entropy regularization is used, while the appendix presents unregularized transport problems without specifying the actual regularized objective or coefficient. Initialization, stopping tolerances, and the chosen update-step procedure are also missing. The recovery hyperparameter tables help, but do not resolve reproducibility of the proposed barycenter computation.

The efficiency claims are only partially supported. Table IV provides a per-image, per-iteration measurement on 64×64 ImageNette without a baseline comparison. The supplementary 14-hour ImageNet figure does not establish comparative cost or separate feature extraction, transport optimization, and image recovery. Matched runtime and memory measurements are needed to substantiate preservation of distribution-matching efficiency.
